subject.title: [Security] CSRF risk via dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback on network-exposed gateway (V-02)

question: Should OpenClaw preserve `gateway.controlUi.dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback` as a documented break-glass mode, harden it with additional browser-side checks, or remove it with an upgrade path?
rationale: Current source shows the fallback is intentional, documented, and audited as dangerous; changing it affects both a security boundary and existing operator configuration behavior.

options.title: Harden the fallback
options.body: Keep the flag default-off, add targeted defenses such as `Sec-Fetch-Site` or a CSRF token where appropriate, and expand tests/docs around DNS-rebinding and same-host fallback behavior.

options.title: Remove with migration
options.body: Delete the fallback and add compatibility-aware doctor/docs guidance for operators who currently rely on it.

options.title: Accept current policy
options.body: Leave the code as-is and rely on critical audit findings plus documentation for operators who deliberately choose the dangerous mode.

recommendation.title: Harden the fallback
recommendation.body: Keep the flag default-off, add targeted defenses such as `Sec-Fetch-Site` or a CSRF token where appropriate, and expand tests/docs around DNS-rebinding and same-host fallback behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the surrounding origin/fallback policy and security posture points to recent gateway hardening work by this person.
